title: Expanding Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure: A Look at California and Beyond
metaTitle: EV Charging Infrastructure 2025: California & LA | Shaffer
metaDescription: EV charging infrastructure expands in 2025: IONNA's rollout, California's leadership, federal funding, and what it means for Los Angeles property owners.
content:
Introduction

The electric vehicle revolution is no longer a distant future scenario: it is happening right now, and the charging infrastructure needed to support it is expanding at an unprecedented pace. From the streets of Los Angeles to communities across the nation, electric vehicle charging stations are becoming as common as traditional gas pumps. As a leading electrical contractor in Los Angeles, Shaffer Construction, Inc. is actively involved in this transformative infrastructure expansion, helping property owners and businesses install the charging solutions they need for today's EV-powered world. In this comprehensive guide, we will explore the dramatic expansion of EV charging infrastructure in 2025, California's leadership role, major national developments, and what these changes mean for Los Angeles property owners and businesses.

California's Continued Dominance in EV Charging

California remains the undisputed leader in electric vehicle adoption and charging infrastructure development. The state has surpassed 150,000 charging stations, representing more EV charging infrastructure than any other state in the nation. This achievement is not accidental: it reflects California's intentional policies, substantial investments, and commitment to reducing transportation-related emissions.

The growth has been remarkable. According to the Alternative Fuels Data Center, California continues to add thousands of new charging ports every month. The state's infrastructure includes everything from Level 1 chargers for residential homes to fast-growing DC fast-charging networks capable of charging an electric vehicle in 20-30 minutes. For Los Angeles specifically, this means easier access to charging for residents, businesses, and fleet operators. Shaffer Construction, Inc. has been instrumental in helping Los Angeles property owners and businesses install both residential and commercial EV chargers as part of this statewide expansion.

The state's success in EV infrastructure is driven by multiple factors, including generous state rebates, streamlined permitting processes, and partnerships between government agencies, utilities, and private contractors. This ecosystem has created unprecedented opportunities for qualified electrical contractors like Shaffer Construction to help property owners make the transition to EV charging infrastructure.

IONNA's Revolutionary National Expansion: The Game Changer of 2025

While California has dominated EV charging, 2025 is witnessing a major nationwide shift with IONNA's national expansion. IONNA, a collaborative charging network backed by eight major automotive manufacturers (BMW, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and Toyota), is deploying over 1,000 new charging bays across North America. This represents the most significant coordinated EV charging expansion by automakers to date.

IONNA's charging stations, called "Rechargeries," are designed to be more than utilitarian charging points. They combine high-speed charging infrastructure with customer amenities, creating a destination-like experience rather than a purely transactional interaction. The network supports both CCS (Combined Charging System) and NACS (North American Charging Standard) connectors, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of electric vehicles. With over 100 sites already contracted as of early 2025, and the network expanding rapidly, this infrastructure will significantly improve national charging coverage and reliability.

For Los Angeles, IONNA's expansion means that the West Coast corridor, already strong in Tesla Superchargers and ChargePoint locations, will have additional high-quality charging options. These new stations will be particularly valuable for long-distance EV travelers and delivery fleet operators who rely on fast, reliable charging to maintain productivity. Shaffer Construction, Inc. understands the importance of infrastructure standardization, and we work with our clients to ensure their charging installations meet evolving national standards.

Federal Infrastructure Investments Supporting Coast-to-Coast Expansion

Beyond California and private networks like IONNA, the federal government continues to invest heavily in EV charging infrastructure. The Department of Energy has awarded hundreds of millions of dollars in grants to build charging networks in underserved regions and support equitable access to EV charging technology. These federal programs ensure that EV charging infrastructure is not limited to wealthy communities or coastal states, but reaches rural areas, disadvantaged neighborhoods, and underserved regions across the country.

This federal support creates a comprehensive ecosystem where state initiatives (like California's aggressive programs), private networks (like IONNA and Tesla), and federal investments work together to build the charging infrastructure of the future. For property owners and businesses in Los Angeles, this means multiple funding sources and incentive programs available to offset the cost of EV charger installation. Shaffer Construction, Inc. helps our clients navigate these incentive programs and secure the best available rebates and grants to make EV charging more affordable.

Los Angeles: A Critical Hub for EV Charging Evolution

Los Angeles deserves special attention in the EV charging narrative because of its unique position as a major metropolitan area with the second-largest EV population in the United States. The city faces specific challenges, dense urban development, limited parking, mixed residential and commercial zoning, that require innovative charging solutions. Multi-family residential buildings, commercial real estate, and fleet operators in Los Angeles must make informed decisions about EV charging infrastructure, and the window for early adoption provides competitive advantages.

As we discussed in our detailed guide on preparing Los Angeles buildings for the EV charging boom, property owners who install charging infrastructure now are positioning themselves for the future. California's Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Title 24) increasingly require new construction and major renovations to include EV charging capability. Existing buildings that proactively install chargers will attract EV-owning tenants, improve property values, and reduce operational energy costs.

Shaffer Construction's experience in Los Angeles electrical infrastructure positions us perfectly to handle these complex charging installations. We manage electrical permits, handle panel upgrades when needed, and ensure installations comply with Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety requirements and California's electrical code.

Charging Technology Standards: Standardization Driving Adoption

One of the most significant developments in the 2024-2025 EV charging landscape is the emergence of standardized charging connectors and communication protocols. The NACS (North American Charging Standard), previously known as the Tesla connector, is being adopted industry-wide. This standardization means that charging networks developed by different manufacturers can interoperate, reducing consumer confusion and increasing the utility of public charging networks.

Most new EV chargers installed today support both CCS and NACS standards, providing maximum compatibility. When Shaffer Construction, Inc. installs EV chargers for Los Angeles property owners, we recommend chargers with multiple connector types to ensure compatibility with the widest range of vehicles. Additionally, smart charging technology allows property owners to schedule charging during off-peak hours, reducing electricity costs and providing grid-balancing benefits.

The evolution of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology also represents an emerging opportunity. Select modern electric vehicles can return power to the grid or building during peak demand periods, potentially generating revenue for property owners. While this technology is still early in adoption, property owners installing chargers today should plan for V2G compatibility to future-proof their installations.

Planning Your EV Charging Installation for Los Angeles

The rapid expansion of EV charging infrastructure and favorable policy environment in California make 2025 an ideal time for Los Angeles property owners and businesses to invest in charging solutions. As we've outlined in our comprehensive guide to deciding on and planning your EV charging project, successful installations require careful planning, professional installation, and proper permitting.

For residential properties in Los Angeles, a Level 2 charger provides optimal balance of convenience and cost. Level 2 chargers typically cost $500-$2,000 installed and can fully charge most vehicles overnight. Many Los Angeles residents qualify for state and utility rebates that significantly reduce this cost. Commercial properties and multi-family buildings should assess their EV charging needs based on tenant demographics, peak charging hours, and available electrical capacity. Our commercial EV charging services include comprehensive assessments, electrical planning, and installation support for property owners managing multiple chargers.

Shaffer Construction, Inc. begins every EV charging project with a thorough electrical assessment. We determine whether your building's electrical service can support the chargers you want to install, identify any panel upgrades needed, and plan the most cost-effective installation route. This planning stage prevents costly mistakes and ensures your installation meets all code requirements.

Addressing Charging Challenges and Infrastructure Gaps

Despite tremendous progress, challenges remain in the EV charging landscape. Cable theft, unreliable chargers in some locations, and variable charging speeds have created friction for EV owners. Additionally, rural areas still lag urban centers in charging availability, and standardized pricing information can be difficult to find. These challenges are gradually being addressed through improved charger design, better network reliability monitoring, and industry standardization efforts.

For Los Angeles property owners, choosing a reliable charging manufacturer and working with experienced installers like Shaffer Construction helps mitigate these issues. We install chargers from manufacturers with strong reputation for reliability and customer support. We also ensure proper electrical grounding, appropriate circuit protection, and weatherproofing to maximize charger longevity and minimize downtime.

Conclusion

The electric vehicle charging infrastructure landscape in 2025 is defined by rapid expansion, major network initiatives, and standardization efforts that are making EV ownership increasingly convenient and practical. California's continued leadership, IONNA's revolutionary network expansion, federal infrastructure investments, and local Los Angeles initiatives collectively create an ecosystem where EV charging infrastructure is becoming ubiquitous.

For Los Angeles property owners and businesses, the question is not whether to install EV charging, but when. Early adopters gain competitive advantages in tenant attraction, property valuation, and operational efficiency. The combination of improving technology, favorable policies, and professional installation services makes 2025 the optimal time to invest in EV charging infrastructure.
